title: Cyclone Arnab slams into India's east coast
lines: A very severe cyclone named Arnab has hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh, in eastern India.
It began making landfall at about half past one on Wednesday morning, near the town of Narsapur.
India's weather department reported winds of one hundred and twenty-five to one hundred and thirty-five kilometres an hour, gusting to one hundred and fifty.
Forecasters warned of a storm surge of up to two and a half metres around Kakinada and Yanam.
Visakhapatnam recorded more than two hundred and sixteen millimetres of rain in a single day.
Authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha moved tens of thousands of people into relief shelters.
Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu said no deaths had been reported by Wednesday morning.
But hundreds of trees were uprooted, power was cut across wide areas, and roads along the coast were damaged.
More than sixty trains were cancelled, flights were disrupted, and schools were closed.
After crossing the coast, Arnab weakened into a severe cyclonic storm, and is moving slowly north-west.
Heavy rain alerts remain in place, and officials are now assessing the damage to crops and homes.
